fha-loan.title: Read FHA premium LTV using a lower appraisal
fha-loan.inputs: $300,000 price; 10% price down; $280,000 appraisal; 6% rate; thirty-year term; automatic ordinary MIP; no other costs or extras.
steps: Use the documented 0.55% annual MIP and thirty-year cap for this model row; it does not establish loan eligibility.
fha-loan.answer: Stated MIP duration cap: 30 years; annual MIP: 0.55%.

fha-loan.title: Add $100 monthly to an FHA loan without changing its premium baseline
fha-loan.inputs: $300,000 price; 3.5% down; 6% rate; thirty-year contract; automatic MIP; $100 extra monthly from month one; no other costs.
steps: Compute P&I on the base loan plus financed upfront MIP.
Add $100 principal after each month’s interest; cap the final payment.
Keep MIP based on the original schedule and stop charging at modeled payoff or its term cap.

va-mortgage.title: Include property costs in a VA payment without monthly MIP
va-mortgage.inputs: $400,000 price; no down; first use; no exemption; 6% for thirty years; fee financed; $4,800 annual tax, $1,200 insurance and $600 HOA.
steps: Compute the 2.15% funding fee and finance it above the $400,000 base loan.
Divide $6,600 total annual ownership allowances by twelve, giving $550 per month.
Add $550 to scheduled P&I without calling it mortgage insurance.

va-mortgage.title: Apply the documented manufactured-home-only prior-use category
va-mortgage.inputs: $400,000 price; no down; 6% for thirty years; prior VA use only for a manufactured home; no established exemption; fee financed; no ownership costs.
steps: Select the narrow Only a manufactured home previous-use category.
The documented purchase rule retains the first-use 2.15% funding fee for this category.
Apply it to the $400,000 base loan; this does not generalize to all repeat use.

house-affordability.title: Allow for 1% annual maintenance within the same housing budget
house-affordability.inputs: $100,000 gross income; $500 monthly other debt; entered 28%/36% ceilings; 20% down; 6% for thirty years; 1.2% property tax; $1,500 annual insurance; 1% annual maintenance; zero HOA.
steps: Compute the tighter entered income-ratio housing budget.
Deduct fixed insurance and allow both percentage tax and maintenance from the solved home value.
Solve the remainder as the mortgage installment; the maintenance percentage is an example, not a standard.

house-affordability.title: Solve a home price with $100,000 cash down and fixed housing allowances
house-affordability.inputs: $2,500 monthly budget; $100,000 cash down; 6% for thirty years; annual tax $3,600, insurance $1,500, maintenance $2,400; $100 monthly HOA.
steps: Fixed non-loan housing allowances total $725 per month.
Use $1,775 for P&I and amortize only the solved price above the fixed $100,000 cash down.
Keep closing costs, reserves and any applicable mortgage insurance separate; the tool does not verify available cash.
house-affordability.answer: Estimated home price: $396,055.12; entered down payment: $100,000.
